title: RAW_UNSCREENED: otar als Fortsetzung oder Recordposten
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED: otar occurs after amount/state fields and before new fields; it may be a continuation relation or a nominal record entry, with direction-sensitive consequences.

design.scope_description: Exact otar contexts f86v5.13, f75r.43 and f115v.5 from GDT769; no new corpus.
design.mechanism: Continuation reading links an earlier field to the next; record reading treats otar as a nominal preparation/field item.
design.unit: otar occurrences in the three complete local frames.
design.contrast: Relational continuation versus nominal record field.
design.prediction: Continuation predicts a following field/state and mixed but licensed transition directions; nominal reading predicts otar can close or occupy a field without requiring a successor state.
concrete_observations: GDT769 places otar after an amount in f86v5.13, between state and close/result at f75r.43, and before an independent process word at f115v.5.
GDT769 reports R05 and R01 role ties, with `bis` as an identity rival.
linked_consequences: A continuation must explain all three written successor configurations without silent endpoints.
A nominal field must recur in line/record positions where no transition is claimed.
design.nearest_rival: A preparation/record noun or endpoint marker such as `bis`.
design.distinguishing_observation: Predeclare successor availability and endpoint status per exact locus; a mixed-direction continuation only survives if each direction has a written target, otherwise the nominal rival remains.
assumption_costs: state changes are not inferred from order alone
design.strongest_likely_failure: GDT769 already finds equal role scores; no written endpoint or successor is independently semantic.
